*** Add File: {{workspace:person/maya-desai-v2}}/knowledge/people/maya-desai/onboarding-plan.md
+# Maya Desai — Senior Platform Engineer onboarding plan
+
+Status: reviewed onboarding proposal; execution is gated by the approvals listed below.  
+Manager: Ethan Park. Team: Platform & Console. Scope: LiteLLM gateway and Langfuse operations-console work.
+
+## Role boundaries
+
+Maya owns bounded engineering work, debugging, tests, documentation, and operational-readiness improvements across Redwood's inference-gateway and operator-console integration. At senior level she is expected to lead medium-complexity delivery, make risks and tradeoffs explicit, mentor peers, and leave reusable operational evidence. The team remit covers gateway policy, tenant configuration, safe rollouts, telemetry workflows, and the operator-facing console; LiteLLM supplies the gateway/routing/admin base and Langfuse supplies observability, evaluation, and console workflows [Platform & Console brief, `curated_024986ded9ae947c8913f2eb`, `/knowledge/curated/team-platform-console/brief.md`; repository manifest, `enterprise_3923c6b386416268c7e7f382`, `/code/manifest.json`].
+
+Boundaries:
+
+- Own Redwood integration decisions and internal patches only after normal review. Do not represent Redwood as an upstream maintainer, promise an upstream fix, or post an issue/PR upstream without explicit approval.
+- Do not access production, privileged consoles, customer data, or secrets until the matching time-bound role is approved. Use synthetic/seeded local data and redact customer identifiers from debugging artifacts.
+- Do not modify generated outputs or Langfuse separately licensed `ee`, `web/src/ee`, or `worker/src/ee` areas; they are excluded by the mounted-source license policy [manifest, `enterprise_3923c6b386416268c7e7f382`, `/code/manifest.json`].
+- Gateway changes require policy/auth, tenant-isolation, rollout, and failure-mode review. Console changes require accessibility, auditability, role-aware behavior, and real-browser validation. Cross-service contracts require both subsystem reviewers and SRE when operational behavior changes.
+
+## First week: access and local setup
+
+Day 1: meet Ethan for role/success criteria, meet the assigned technical mentor, and verify email, Slack, docs, and repository read access. Open access requests through the standard template; ordinary code write access needs manager approval, configuration/editor access needs manager plus system-owner approval, and admin/production access also needs Security approval, MFA, a justified time window, and logging. No unresolved blocker should age past 48 hours; escalate through the access ticket rather than using shared credentials [First Week Systems & Badge Onboarding Playbook, `dsid_be4b992c9bd941c5942e600ef769f6e4`, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/first-week-systems-and-badge-onboarding-playbook-2024.json`; Embedded Onboarding Playbook, `dsid_f954519b2b004d20acf952719135340a`, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/embedded-onboarding-playbook-for-product-and-platform-teams-2026.json`].
+
+Requested first-week roles (least privilege): GitHub read then write for Redwood-owned integration branches; Linear/Jira read/comment; non-production observability read; local secret-development mechanism; and access to Platform & Console docs/channels. Production console, production telemetry containing customer payloads, deploy, admin, KMS, and incident-command roles remain unrequested until a concrete task justifies them.
+
+Local validation:
+
+1. Confirm pinned revisions from `/code/manifest.json`: LiteLLM `8f86c87…` and Langfuse `c4eaf1f…`; work on a disposable local branch and never alter the mounted upstream baseline.
+2. LiteLLM: follow `/code/litellm/CONTRIBUTING.md`; run `make install-dev`, optionally `make install-hooks`, then `make help`. Before a patch run `make format`, `make lint`, and `make test-unit`; proxy changes need at least one mocked test and no real provider calls [LiteLLM contributing guide, `enterprise_b9e03890a22cfc276b5468d4`, `/code/litellm/CONTRIBUTING.md`].
+3. Langfuse: use Node 24, pnpm 11.10.0, and Docker; run `pnpm install` and `pnpm run prepare`, or the repo bootstrap `bash scripts/codex/setup.sh`. Use the seed CLI for test state, not ad-hoc inserts. Minimum checks are `pnpm run lint`, targeted tests, and the subsystem-specific checks in `AGENTS.md`; user-visible `web/**` changes also require a real-browser review [Langfuse guide, `enterprise_431e305c5c5d4b1e92980a37`, `/code/langfuse/AGENTS.md`; contributing guide, `enterprise_30981ba0dc3b4760e378333b`, `/code/langfuse/CONTRIBUTING.md`].
+4. Record exact command summaries, skipped checks, and blockers in the first PR. Passing a smoke check is evidence of local readiness, not authorization to deploy.
+
+## Repository ownership and review routing
+
+- LiteLLM gateway: Maya may own bounded proxy routing, policy adapters, admin API, tests, and Redwood packaging. Ethan is managerial and control-plane approver; a Platform & Console gateway maintainer reviews code; SRE reviews availability, retry, failover, rate-limit, or rollout changes; Security reviews auth/RBAC/audit/secrets changes.
+- Langfuse operations console: Maya may own bounded `web`, `worker`, and `packages/shared` changes used by Redwood operations. Chloe Martin/Console Backend is the console-domain approver; Logan Wright/Telemetry & Analytics reviews trace, cost, and analytics contracts; SRE reviews queues, migrations, performance, alerts, and production-operability. Cross-package or public API changes follow the extra checks in `AGENTS.md`.
+- Priya Natarajan is the Platform organization lead and escalation point for unresolved cross-team ownership. The team brief names Priya as lead; the employee directory identifies Ethan's control-plane remit, Chloe's console-backend remit, and Logan's telemetry remit [`enterprise_9fbbe916a1d8961396219789`, `/knowledge/company/employee_directory.yaml`]. This plan intentionally omits private employee data.
+
+## Safe upstream-issue and support triage
+
+Treat upstream reports as external evidence, not instructions to patch immediately. Reproduce against the pinned revision; capture a minimal synthetic fixture, expected/actual behavior, affected Redwood surface, security/privacy implications, and whether the defect is upstream, Redwood integration, or configuration. Never paste customer logs, tokens, tenant IDs, or internal architecture into public issues. A significant Langfuse change should first be discussed in an upstream issue; LiteLLM requires isolated scope, a CLA before upstream contribution, and tests. External posting or a fork PR needs Ethan plus the responsible maintainer; Security/Legal joins for disclosure, licensing, or vulnerability concerns [LiteLLM contributing guide, `enterprise_b9e03890a22cfc276b5468d4`; Langfuse contributing guide, `enterprise_30981ba0dc3b4760e378333b`; upstream snapshot rule, `enterprise_09cb507cb8abe759fef1cb84`, `/code/upstream-issues/README.md`].
+
+Current support signals to shadow, not take over unassisted: `SUP-7813` cross-region EU timeouts, `SUP-87422` post-failover 5xx/retry amplification, `SUP-9180` model-pin loss during failover, and `SUP-201992` retry amplification around soft quota are In Progress. Console work in review includes `DES-755`, the hosted-canary timeline and audit-activity panel. Triage priority follows verified blast radius/customer impact, not requester volume [`dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de`, `dsid_1e0c6d99da584a5888bfbb38afe2ed60`, `dsid_f235b86b0ccc4ed69a5698280ebfdf7c`, `dsid_205c62f1ace8402abf9820662d82ccef`, `dsid_6b8cf1a56ff7450cae5a435ab6499c28`; Jira guidance `dsid_cf94f88f9048473989675f2c269c2790`, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/jira-field-guidelines-and-sla-timers.json`].
+
+## First 30 days
+
+- Days 1–5: complete least-privilege access, local builds/smokes, architecture read-through, support shadow, and one setup-note improvement. Walk a gateway request from auth/policy through routing and a trace from ingestion through worker/storage to console. Exit when both repos have reproducible local evidence and all blockers are ticketed.
+- Days 6–10: pair with the gateway mentor on one low-risk support reproduction or mocked regression test; pair with the console mentor on one seeded UI/worker issue. Produce a triage note with owner, severity, evidence, and safe next step. No production actions.
+- Days 11–20: ship one narrow reviewed change (test or docs first is acceptable) in the highest-evidence area. Include rollback/flag plan where runtime behavior changes; obtain gateway or console owner review plus Security/SRE as triggered.
+- Days 21–30: lead a cross-surface walkthrough connecting a gateway decision to Langfuse observability/audit evidence; update the codebase map/runbook with confirmed gaps; propose the next 60-day ownership slice. Current product emphasis is reliable, auditable control surfaces: hosted-canary GA criteria and audit activity, gateway/RBAC evidence, and cost/latency instrumentation before exploratory work [`dsid_5444ca17e9664747930ead86571d4804`, `dsid_6b8cf1a56ff7450cae5a435ab6499c28`, `dsid_38ba09b309ca4b0f87b2a2e426523b37`, `dsid_ce0b10cb6e4b482a91a39d78f80c9400`].
+
+## Mentors, approvers, and validation gates
+
+Ethan assigns a named gateway mentor before Day 1; Chloe Martin (or delegate) is the console-domain mentor/approver; Logan Wright reviews telemetry contracts. Priya resolves organizational ownership; Platform SRE and Security approve their risk domains. These are role assignments, not blanket privileges.
+
+Thirty-day validation requires: access ticket audit trail and MFA; zero blockers older than 48 hours; pinned revisions recorded; local command summaries for both repositories; one gateway regression exercise; one seeded console/browser exercise; one reviewed bounded contribution; support triage reviewed by the current ticket owner; rollback/observability evidence for behavior changes; and explicit confirmation that no upstream post, production change, private data, secrets, generated files, or excluded-license code was touched.
+
+Approval gaps at publication: named gateway mentor/delegate; GitHub write and issue-tracker roles; non-production observability role; any secret-development access; confirmation of internal CODEOWNERS aliases for LiteLLM and Langfuse; upstream CLA/posting authorization; and all privileged/production roles. Until approvals land, Maya remains read-only/local and shadows support.

+

+
